intro.title: useImperativeHandle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with a custom input component that uses the useImperativeHandle hook to expose a method to its parent. You will learn how useImperativeHandle allows a child component to define custom functions that a parent can call directly, similar to using a ref. The main technologies involved are Vue's Composition API with the ref and defineExpose functions. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to controlling child component behavior from a parent in Vue.
intro.usecase: In Vue applications, exposing child component methods to parent components is essential for complex UI interactions. This pattern appears in form validation scenarios where a parent needs to trigger validation across multiple child input components, or in dashboard widgets where a parent container needs to programmatically refresh specific chart components. Developers use this approach when building interactive data tables with custom filtering controls, modal dialogs that need external open/close triggers, or complex multi-step forms where navigation logic resides in a parent component but needs to manipulate child step components directly.
